alreadyShipped.capability: Source-preserving OCR with reviewable recognition evidence and positioned invisible searchable text.
Visual mixed PDF/image assembly with insert/replace, duplex interleaving, blank pages, ordering, visual crop, and undo/redo.
Intent-aware source/output fidelity gating before publication.

baseline.staleGapPolicy: Current source and current product contracts override historical gap lists.

items.title: Layout-aware editable PDF to DOCX export
items.outcome: Export materially useful editable DOCX files that retain paragraph order, common tables, images, page breaks, and reliable styling better than the current text-only path.
evidence: src/professional/docx.ts: buildTextDocx extracts page text into simple paragraphs
README.md: DOCX export is explicitly text-only and not layout-faithful
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md: DOCX export prioritizes editable text over visual fidelity
acceptance: Paragraph/read-order reconstruction and page breaks survive export for the qualified corpus.
Common detected tables become editable Word tables instead of flattened plain text.
Supported source images are included with deterministic ordering or anchoring.
Supported text styling is retained when source evidence is reliable.
Ambiguous or unsupported layout is reported explicitly rather than silently advertised as faithful.
Conversion remains browser-local and works offline after the app is installed.

items.title: Complex-script existing-text editing
items.outcome: Safely edit qualified shaping-dependent scripts, starting with Arabic/RTL, using real shaping and bidi instead of appearance-only fallback.
evidence: KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md: Arabic, Indic, RTL and shaping-dependent scripts remain appearance-only fallback
docs/product/P1_EXISTING_TEXT_EDITING_EXCELLENCE.md: broader script/font coverage requires a real shaping/font path
acceptance: The implementation defines an explicit qualified-script matrix rather than claiming universal Unicode editing.
Arabic/RTL edits use correct bidi ordering and shaping in fixed-box reconstruction.
Font/glyph coverage is validated before Apply/export and missing coverage fails closed.
Qualified output embeds or references a deterministic usable font path without corrupt substitution.
Multilingual browser and source/output fidelity fixtures cover shaping, punctuation, mixed-direction text, Undo/Redo, export, and reopen.

items.title: Structure-preserving target-size compression
items.outcome: Let users request a realistic output size while retaining searchable/vector/interactive PDF structure whenever feasible.
evidence: src/views/CompressionPage.tsx: current choices are lossless optimization or fixed raster profiles
docs/EVERYDAY_PDF_WORKFLOWS.md: reliable target-size compression remains a separate improvement
acceptance: Users can specify a target size and preservation preference.
The optimizer uses bounded attempts and prioritizes safe structural/image optimization before destructive raster fallback.
Before/after bytes and a preservation summary are shown for the selected result.
Unattainable targets return an explicit best-achieved result or refusal instead of a false success.
Outputs that are larger than the source are not labelled successful compression.

items.title: Batch parity and encrypted-queue ergonomics
items.outcome: Make reusable Batch workflows cover more high-value standalone tasks and handle encrypted queue items safely.
evidence: src/types/batch.ts: Batch schema v3 exposes a bounded ten-step operation set
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md: Batch does not expose every standalone tool
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md: per-file password prompts for encrypted queue items remain missing
acceptance: A checked capability matrix identifies safely composable standalone tasks and explicit non-Batch boundaries.
Highest-value missing composable operations are added with deterministic recipe semantics.
Encrypted queue items can request per-file session-only credentials without persistence or diagnostic leakage.
Recipe/input changes invalidate stale outputs deterministically.
Terminal or multi-output steps have explicit output naming, ZIP/result semantics, and ordering.

items.title: Deep native-content fidelity
items.outcome: Expand safe existing-content editing into currently conservative image/vector/table/reflow classes without claiming universal content-stream rewriting.
evidence: KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md: image masks, clipping, blend modes, and shared-image semantics are not universally preserved
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md: vector detection omits arbitrary nested paths, clipping stacks, shadings, patterns, and inherited graphics state
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md: table detection does not understand every merged-cell or semantic table structure
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md: paragraph reflow across neighboring objects, columns, and pages remains bounded
acceptance: Every newly supported object class has a deterministic detection/capability rule and fail-closed unsupported state.
Qualified image edits preserve required mask/clipping/blend/shared-resource semantics for their fixture class.
Qualified vector edits preserve required graphics-state semantics for their fixture class.
Qualified irregular/merged table edits preserve cell geometry and unaffected content.
Any cross-region text reflow uses deterministic blocker/follower rules and never silently crosses an unsupported flow boundary.
Source/output fidelity fixtures detect collateral changes to untouched content.

items.title: Compatibility and human/device qualification
items.outcome: Qualify v7.2 capabilities on difficult real PDFs, external readers, and representative physical devices before release.
evidence: KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md: external-reader, mobile, large-corpus, malformed-file, and adversarial validation remains required for release confidence
GitHub issue #62: physical-device field observations remain an explicit evidence class
acceptance: Qualification includes malformed, scanned, form-heavy, encrypted, signed, multilingual, and large real-world cases relevant to v7.2 changes.
External-reader results are recorded against exact output artifact identity.
Physical phone/tablet/installed-PWA observations are recorded for affected supported workflows.
Human/device evidence is not synthesized from automation.
Unresolved compatibility or data-loss failures block release qualification.

items.title: DOCX to PDF import
items.outcome: Determine whether a local structured DOCX-to-PDF path can reuse the V72-01 document model without degrading into falsely labelled screenshot conversion.
evidence: Current product exports DOCX but does not provide qualified layout-aware DOCX import
acceptance: Promotion requires a local/offline architecture and a corpus for paragraphs, tables, images, lists, page geometry, and unsupported-feature disclosure.

items.title: Independent PDF/A validation integration
items.outcome: Determine whether local independent validation can strengthen current PDF/A candidate preparation into better conformance evidence.
evidence: KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md: PDF/A output is candidate preparation, not an ISO conformance certificate
acceptance: Promotion requires a standards-validating engine, bounded runtime cost, explicit supported profiles, and no normal-startup penalty.

items.title: Dedicated two-pointer document zoom
items.outcome: Determine whether canvas-level pinch zoom materially improves mobile editing without harming browser or accessibility zoom.
evidence: KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md: a dedicated two-pointer document-zoom gesture is not implemented
acceptance: Promotion requires physical phone/tablet usability evidence and no regression to browser accessibility zoom.

items.title: Bidirectional XLSX/PPTX and broad Office-suite parity
items.reason: Too broad for v7.2 and likely to force low-fidelity claims or a server dependency before the narrower DOCX model is proven.

items.title: Browser certificate-store and PAdES signing
items.outcome: Certificate-backed cryptographic signing in the consumer browser build.
items.reason: Native certificate stores, PKCS#11 and HSM integration remain outside the browser-local consumer runtime boundary.

items.title: Automatic full PDF/UA reconstruction
items.outcome: Infer a complete semantic accessibility tree from arbitrary visual PDFs.
items.reason: Current evidence supports inspection and bounded repairs, not reliable universal semantic reconstruction.

items.title: Unrestricted PDF content-stream rewriting and enterprise/native platform expansion
items.outcome: Universal object rewriting plus desktop-companion, enterprise fleet, federation, or zero-trust expansion.
items.reason: This conflicts with the bounded consumer/local-first v7.2 objective and would expand risk, dependencies, and product complexity without a concrete release need.
